next.name: GOLD LOCUST
next.headline: GOLD LOCUST: the group also tracked as FIN7 and Carbanak, from USB mailings to loader malware
next.in_short: Secureworks tracks GOLD LOCUST, which the catalogue also lists as FIN7 and Carbanak. Reports describe mailed USB drives, the JSSLoader malware and a Carbanak backdoor. Some researchers tie its tools to ransomware cases.

sentences.t: GOLD LOCUST is the name Secureworks uses for this actor.
The catalogue lists these other names: Anunak, Carbanak, Carbon Spider, FIN7 and Silicon.
Carbanak is the one tool the catalogue names for the actor.
An FBI alert, as reported by BleepingComputer, says FIN7 mailed packages through USPS to businesses in the retail, restaurant and hotel industries.
BleepingComputer also reports that Fin7 hacked Saks Fifth Avenue and Lord & Taylor in 2018 to steal payment card information.
In the mailed packages, the USB drives were set up to act as a keyboard. They typed commands to fetch the GRIFFON malware. One package used a gift card as bait.
Morphisec describes a FIN7 chain that starts with a phishing campaign. A VBScript stage runs in memory. A scheduled task with a delay then runs a module. A script loads Carbanak directly into memory.
Sentinel Labs links the sellers of the AvNeutralizer tool to the FIN7 cluster with high confidence, as Harfanglab cites it. The tool uses vulnerable drivers to stop security processes.
Harfanglab says the developers of the PackXOR packer might be connected to the FIN7 cluster. It adds that the packer appears to be used for activity unrelated to FIN7.
Rapid7 assesses that the developers of a Java malware family are likely initial access brokers. It says they potentially provided access to Black Basta and/or FIN7 affiliates.
Morphisec says it intercepted a JSSLoader attack chain in a customer network in December 2020. It reports that FIN7 uses JSSLoader.
BleepingComputer's report on the FBI alert about the USB mailings was published on 27 March 2020.
Malwarebytes attributes a late-June malspam campaign to FIN7. It dropped JSSLoader, a rewrite with added data exfiltration, plus a second payload written in .NET. The post is dated 15 August 2022.
SentinelLABS reported on 3 November 2022 that Black Basta attacks deploy custom EDR evasion tools it ties to FIN7.
Do not plug in USB drives that arrive unasked, and treat unexpected invoice attachments with care.
